They also took most of the weapons and equipment, and the units that withdrew from the Brcko front line took a significant amount along with them. They kept quite a lot of weapons in unnecessary locations. For example, some mortars are still in the hospital compound. All of this led to a series of incidents with which the command of the Brcko Brigade was unable to deal efficiently. How does this fit into what you yourself knew?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I said similar things.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have page 5 and then 6. First 5 in English and 9 in Serbian. Fine. We have it in Serbian already. This is the right page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first page of the second paragraph, "Certain formations ..."

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You want me to read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: "Certain formations have established their warehouses and looted goods in Brcko as well as Bijeljina. Like, for example, the special unit in the duty-free zone. This unit has even produced its own seal so that it could issue appropriate documentation. The command of the unit believes it should have its own till, its own current account, and, as was said earlier, it should organise the public security station, influence the civilian political leadership, the military police and the entire command structure." Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: "It is important to mention that the unit carried out an attack on the public security station (senior organs have been informed of it). All these activities have been accompanied by rapes, unauthorised interrogations, the issuing of dubious permits to leave town (probably for a hefty fee), and there are indications that in the most drastic cases, members of unknown formations have executed people."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the position of the authorities vis-a-vis such groups and formations in terms of what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that we tried any which way to get ride of them, and only when reinforcements came from the top of the Republika Srpska MUP we managed to chase them away, and until that point all of us living in Brcko had to put up with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about regular passes? What were they used for by those moving through the territory?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: If someone needed to go, for example, to the Military Medical Academy in Belgrade or to do something in Bijeljina, then they relied on the passes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The person who was issued with such a certificate, could they discard of it, throw it away or abuse it in some other way?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D1412, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were military conscripts free to move around without appropriate permits?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D1412. Thank you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is a document of the Federal Ministry of the Interior. The date is the 8th of August. That is a report on providing expert assistance to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP. You were asked about it already today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 7 in English and in Serbian page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the last paragraph, "In the area of Brcko..." Please read it out.

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: "In the area of Brcko there was a group of Red Berets active headed by Captain Dragan. Rade and Bozo Bozic, the brothers were particularly exposed, stood out, as well as the group of Zivojin ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please. The next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on the bottom part. I can't read out the beginning. It probably says "Crnogorac Ivanovic." "Which comprised some 40 members who presented themselves as Serbian MUP officials. Ivanovic and his group had IDs and the stamp of the Krajina MUP as well as the official IDs of the Serbian MUP. Under threat, they took 22 IDs from the public security station. Upon their arrival in Brcko, the Ivanovic group undertook certain tasks upon them without any authorisation which otherwise belonged -- were in the remit of the MUP, such as searches of premises, commandeering vehicles, et cetera. They beat regular policemen and mistreated them up to the point of using force. Such conduct was also exerted in the presence of military officers and concerning civilians."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go two lines down, "The Red Berets ..."

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: "The Red Berets of Captain Dragan commanded by Rade Bozic, inter alia, burst into the public security station in Brcko and held hostage the municipal president and the Chief of Staff of the 1st Posavina Brigade, I believe. They threatened them and blackmailed them, telling they would be liquidated unless the three arrested members are released from detention in Bijeljina. On another occasion, the Bozic brothers and the Red Berets burst into the police station where they broke into the safe and took away money, communications equipment, weapons" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us stop here. I don't see the point of asking the witness to read out the document which has been already admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're right, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me just say this: In line 5 it reads that the authorities were afraid for their own lives, too, or those from the authorities. Can you tell us who held power in Brcko before Mico Davidovic arrived?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The Red Berets and some such people. Davidovic drove all of them out. He had them arrested, and they had to leave the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It was suggested to you in one of the questions that the municipal authorities in the Serb municipality of Brcko actually found it appropriate to have paramilitary units driving Muslims out and arresting them, and only later, the authorities became dissatisfied with their conduct. Can you tell us about the sequence of events. When and how did the Muslims leave Brcko at the time these units arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please begin again because there was an overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because of overlapping, the interpreters were not able to hear you, so could you start again your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I said already that on the 30th of April, all of us residing in Brcko tried to go away from there any which way possible, and in the course of those few days or weeks, it was a deserted town. It was definitely fruitful ground for such paramilitary formations to loot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did any Muslims remain living in your -- or in the Serbian part of Brcko municipality, such as a village or in the town itself, and until when?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: They reside there even today. They lived there throughout. Many people of different ethnicities lived in that Serbian part of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about during the war?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: During the war as well. There were many killed and wounded of all ethnicities during the war in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any Muslims in the VRS from Brcko?

utterances.speaker: PERO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There were. There were even killed VRS fighters from there and their families enjoyed the same rights as those of all other fighters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Markovic, and thank you for everything you have done for all three peoples and for carrying out the duties of the bodies of authority in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Markovic. Thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go. Have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before the adjournment, the Chamber will issue an oral ruling on the accused's "Motion for Modification of Segregation Regime with Witness Milan Martic" filed on the 1st of March, 2013, in which the accused moves for a variation of the terms of the Chamber's order for the temporary transfer of a detained witness issued confidentially on the 8th of January, 2013. The Chamber recalls that it ordered, inter alia, that (i) Martic be kept segregated at the UNDU from the accused, and (ii) no contact take place either inside or outside the UNDU between Martic and the accused other than is necessary for purposes of witness proofing. In the motion, the accused requests that his segregation from Martic only be limited to the period in which Martic is giving evidence as there is no reason why he should not have contact with Martic either prior to or after his testimony. Earlier this morning, the Office of the Prosecutor orally informed the Chamber that it opposes the motion, noting that the motion is effectively a motion for reconsideration and that the accused has failed to meet the relevant standard. As a preliminary matter, the Chamber considers that the motion is in fact a motion for reconsideration of the 8th of January order. The Chamber first reminds the accused that when filing motions which are essentially requests for reconsideration, he must address the applicable legal standard as opposed to simply avoiding the issue altogether. In the present case, the Chamber recalls that in its 8th of January order, it explicitly provided for proofing and for the witness's transfer to the UNDU a week prior to his expected testimony, then scheduled for the week of 4th of March, as it deemed this time period sufficient for the purpose of preparing a Rule 92 ter statement and disclosing it to the Prosecution in a timely manner. The Chamber did not impose any limits on the proofing that the accused may deem necessary within the course of boundaries of UNDU organisational constraints and outside of court hearings. However, the Chamber considered that segregation other than for proofing purposes was warranted in this case to preserve the integrity of Martic's forthcoming testimony. This continues to be the case. The Chamber thus considers that the accused does not demonstrate either a clear error in reasoning or particular circumstances justifying that the 8th of January order be reconsidered in order to prevent an injustice and therefore denies the motion. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does it also mean that there are no restrictions after his testimony, because there's no reference to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think that our ruling did deal with that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Basically I think it's a matter for the Detention Unit. If necessary, the Chamber will come back to the issue. The hearing is adjourned.
